In [[mathematics]], a '''3-step group''' is a special sort of [[group (mathematics)|group]] of [[Fitting length]] at most 3, that is used in the classification of [[CN group]]s and in the [[Feit–Thompson theorem]]. The definition of a 3-step group in these two cases is slightly different.

==CN groups==

In the theory of CN groups, a 3-step group (for some [[prime number|prime]] ''p'') is a group such that:
*{{math|''G'' {{=}} O<sub>''p'',''p{{'}}'',''p''</sub>(''G'')}}
*{{math|O<sub>''p'',''p''{{prime}}</sub>(''G'')}} is a [[Frobenius group]] with kernel {{math|O<sub>''p''</sub>(''G'')}}
*{{math|''G''/O<sub>''p''</sub>(''G'')}} is a Frobenius group with kernel {{math|O<sub>''p'',''p''{{prime}}</sub>(''G'')/O<sub>''p''</sub>(''G'')}}

Any 3-step group is a [[solvable group|solvable]] CN-group, and conversely any solvable CN-group is either [[nilpotent group|nilpotent]], or a Frobenius group, or a 3-step group.

Example: the [[symmetric group]] ''S''<sub>4</sub> is a 3-step group for the prime {{math|''p'' {{=}} 2}}.

==Odd order groups==

{{harvtxt|Feit|Thompson|1963|loc=p.780}} defined a three-step group to be a group ''G'' satisfying the following conditions:
*The derived group of ''G'' is a Hall subgroup with a cyclic complement ''Q''.
*If ''H'' is the maximal normal nilpotent Hall subgroup of ''G'', then ''G''{{prime}}{{prime}}⊆''H''C<sub>''G''</sub>(''H'')⊆''G''{{prime}} and ''H''C<sub>''G''</sub> is nilpotent and ''H'' is noncyclic.
*For ''q''∈''Q'' nontrivial, C<sub>''G''</sub>(''q'') is cyclic and non-trivial and independent of ''q''.
